title: Does Your Building's Access-Controlled Door Have a Current IQP Inspection?
description: Under the New Zealand Building Act, access-controlled doors listed on a building's compliance schedule require regular inspection by an Independently Qualified Person (IQP). Many building owners and facility managers don't realise this obligation applies to them — or that an expired IQP inspection can affect their building warrant of fitness. Red Wolf is registered to carry out IQP inspections across Wellington and Auckland. Here is what the inspection covers, how often it is required, and what to expect.

title: What NZSA Accreditation Actually Requires — and Why It Matters for Your Next Tender
description: NZSA accreditation is not a box-tick. It requires an annual self-audit assessed by independent auditors, minimum insurance levels, adherence to a Code of Ethical Conduct, and demonstrated compliance with industry standards. For organisations evaluating security providers through a tender or procurement process, it is one of the most reliable indicators of operational quality. Red Wolf has held NZSA accreditation since our founding. Here is what it covers and the questions you should ask any prospective provider.

title: It Is Security Awareness Month — What Is the One Physical Security Gap Your Business Should Fix This October?
description: October is Security Awareness Month — and while most of the conversation focuses on cyber, physical security gaps are just as common and often just as costly. Tailgating into secured areas, propped doors, unmonitored visitor access, and outdated credentials are issues we find in almost every building assessment we carry out. This month we are sharing practical fixes for the most common physical security oversights. What is the one thing on your list? Drop it in the comments.
